events.excerpt: An American AI lab has re-educated Qwen3.8-27B, a popular open-weight large language model from Alibaba, so the software forgets its Chinese ancestry. Nous Research, an Austin, Texas-based AI lab, has subjected the model to re-education through training, not to be confused with China's " Re-education Through Labor " system. With the help of a post-training process, Qwen3.8-27B has been reborn under the name Arete "to reinforce Western values on a Chinese-trained model." What qualifies as a "Western value" remains open to interpretation. "Open-weight Chinese models are among the strongest available, but they ship with state-aligned behavior baked into the weights," Nous Research wrote in a blog post . Your correspondent tested this with a variant model, Qwen3.8-27B-MLX-6bit, locally. Asked about events during 1989 in Tiananmen Square, the model either refused to discuss the topic or provided euphemistic response. What's perhaps more surprising is that Anthropic claims operators affiliated with Alibaba's Qwen lab used outputs from its Claude models to train competing AI models via distillation . Nous Research, maker of the Hermes Agent , cites that sort of censorship as a risk for users of AI models trained in China. The concern comes amid broader scrutiny of Chinese influence in t
events.headline: Alibaba's Qwen3.8 re-educated with a more Western worldview

events.excerpt: Author: Daemon Minwar Category: Economics / Mechanism Design TL;DR We propose WARCoin , a deterministic, exploit-resistant 1:1 USD stablecoin architecture designed to eliminate infinite-mint bugs, cross-collateral contagion, and replay vectors. Instead of monolithic balance mappings, WARCoin enforces a USD-only ingress firewall , burn-on-egress serial invalidation , and 7 daily color-coded ring buckets ( 1,000 serials/bucket, #1 – #1,000 ) bounded by a strict 10^9 global supply invariant. 1. Threat Model & Motivation Standard ERC-20 stablecoins rely on unbounded integer storage slots ( mapping(address => uint256) ). If a minting authority is compromised or a bridge/collateral contract is exploited, attackers can mint arbitrary unbacked supply or contaminate reserves with toxic collateral. WARCoin mitigates these vectors at the state-transition level by enforcing finite, serialized issuance slots and strict asset isolation. 2. Core Protocol Architecture A. Ingress / Egress Asset Firewall Strict USD-Only Ingress: The minting router reverts on any non-USD asset deposit ( require(asset == USD) ). External crypto-assets are rejected at the gateway to prevent collateral contagion. Burn-on-Egress Invalidation: Outbound transfers or swaps into external tokens immediately burn the underly

events.excerpt: When Radio Shack introduced the Color Computer 3 in 1986, it brought some major improvements to its popular line of home computers. With better graphics, support for more memory, and an improved video system, the CoCo 3 was a big step up from its predecessors. Unfortunately, owners of the original CoCo and CoCo 2 had no way to upgrade their existing machines. Getting those new capabilities meant buying an entirely new computer. Four decades later, developer Felipe Antoniosi is finally offering an alternative with CoCoTANG, an open source upgrade that brings many of the CoCo 3's features to older Color Computers. The project is built around a Sipeed Tang Nano 20K FPGA development board, which recreates the CoCo 3's Graphics, Interrupt, Memory Enhancement (GIME) chip in programmable logic. Rather than replacing the entire computer with an emulator, CoCoTANG works alongside the original Motorola MC6809E processor and motherboard Peripheral Interface Adapters. One of the biggest benefits of using an FPGA is that it allows for 8 MB of RAM, far more than the 512 KB an original CoCo 3 could accommodate. CoCoTANG also adds the CoCo 3's enhanced graphics capabilities, making it possible to run software that takes advantage of the newer computer's display modes. The video system gets some
events.headline: It's Never Too Late to Upgrade Your CoCo

Azure served 63% of migrated-service reads, 66% of monolith reads, and 52% of Git reads. events.excerpt: Bitcoin Magazine DOJ Wins Court Authority to Seize $1.2 Billion of North Korea’s Stolen Binance Crypto as Freezes Top $2.7 Billion The DOJ said Thursday it has court authority to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion in cryptocurrency stolen from Binance, part of a freeze of more than $2.7 billion that officials said halted about half of North Korea’s October exchange heist. In a Thursday announcement, the department said that on or about Oct. 29, members of the North Korean military, referred to by the FBI as TraderTraitor, stole more than $6 billion worth of virtual assets from Binance. That is below the $6.34 billion figure Binance has covered since the attack. Binance said it had completed coverage of the assets hit in the breach, replacing the tokens from company funds rather than by recovering the stolen coins. Those are separate tracks: the DOJ is trying to interdict what was taken, while the exchange has said users were made whole from its Secure Asset Fund for Users, a portion of its futures insurance fund and its treasury. Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the DOJ’s Criminal Division said the department and its partners were able to “immediately halt about half of this historic breach” by freezing stolen assets “before they got beyond law enforcement reach.

events.excerpt: Remember the movie Big ? It came out in 1988 and starred Tom Hanks. With almost 40 years of hindsight, I think it is safe to say that the most memorable part of the film was the Zoltar fortune-telling machine that kicks off the entire plot (and definitely not the problematic romantic relationship). I’m not entirely sure how common those were in real life before the movie came out, but the movie cemented the concept in pop culture. To pay homage to that, Robert (AKA Oh well why not) built his own fortune teller and it is, frankly, kind of creepy. Meet Lilith. This shares many traits with Zoltar from Big — primarily that it is an arcade cabinet-size machine, that it contains a humanoid animatronic figure, and that it provides fortunes. But it differs in aesthetics and in how it conveys fortunes. In Big , Zoltar provides a fortune in the form of a printed slip of paper. That made sense for the technology of the era and also for the movie’s plot. But Robert didn’t have those constraints, so he made his machine read the fortunes out loud. The artificial psychic inside the box is also far more sophisticated. Zoltar was a very simple animatronic — in real life, it would likely be entirely electromechanical. events.excerpt: In a significant update to its guidelines for prostate cancer screening, the American Cancer Society is now recommending that men get routinely screened for prostate cancer with a PSA (prostate-specific antigen) test. Men at average risk should get a PSA test every two years from age 50 to 69, according to the new guidelines released Thursday. Men considered at high risk due to race and family history should start testing earlier, at 45, and most are recommended to get tested every year. Specifically, yearly testing starting at age 45 is recommended for all Black men, who have higher rates of prostate cancer. Non-Black men should also get yearly testing starting at 45 if a close relative was diagnosed with prostate cancer before age 65, or if more than one of their relatives has had prostate cancer. On the other hand, if only one close relative was diagnosed with prostate cancer and it was diagnosed at age 65 or older, non-Black men in this case should start PSA screening at 45, but are recommended to get testing only every two years. Read full article Comments
events.headline: In reversal, American Cancer Society urges routine prostate cancer screening

events.excerpt: How many times this week did you re-explain the same task to an agent? How many times did you ask your colleague with deep institutional knowledge how to solve a specific problem? That context shouldn’t be lost in a chat or locked in one person’s head. Agent skills let you capture repeatable instructions so you and your agents can reuse them. The skill you write for yourself tonight can later become part of a team’s pipeline. An agent skill is a versioned directory centered on a SKILL.md file that describes when and how to do a repeatable task. You can share those instructions across agents, but the environment still needs to provide the tools, credentials, and permissions to carry them out. A skill can describe how to query a database, for example, but it doesn’t grant access to that database. I covered this topic live with Shishir Tewari, Senior Manager, Data Engineering at Procore, during GitHub Universe 2026. Our session was titled “Build once, run on any agent: a practical guide to agent skills” . Define one job and when it applies A skill works best when it has a clear job, input, and output. For example, let’s say you’re building an agent that checks AI-generated changes against the original request. If the same agent assesses its own work, its explanation might influence

events.excerpt: The maker community has many traditions that I love and among my favorites is the electronic conference badge. Sometimes, those are badges provided by the organizers of the conference — that is the case with Hackaday Supercons, for example. But if badges aren’t provided, attendees still like to build their own. That’s exactly what Clem Mayer did for his Community Badge , which doubles as a handheld game console. Like most badges, the Community Badge doesn’t have an enclosure. It is just components on a PCB, so everything is in view. That PCB has a lanyard loop at the top, so the badge can be worn around the neck, as is the tradition. It also has an SAO ( Simple Add-On) header, for connecting additional modules. That is also tradition. What isn’t necessarily tradition — though it certainly isn’t uncommon — is the functionality. The Community Badge can act as a badge, to display the wearer’s name and such. But when the conference is done for the night and it is time to relax, it can also act as a game console. It even as a d-pad and A/B buttons for exactly that reason. To prove its gaming validity, Mayer created six games that run on the Community Badge: Millipeter, Blockinger, Brechaus, Personal Space Invaders (strange how you find out later) , Frickin Bird, and Roadkill . events.headline: This DIY Conference Badge Doubles As a Handheld Game Console

events.excerpt: If you've ever said something unkind to a chatbot, you're hardly alone. According to Searchable , a company that tracks AI search visibility, 33 percent of US chatbot users swear at or insult their LLMs. Anthropic sees this as a serious problem and has just implemented a new usage policy that prohibits sustained, needless cruelty toward Claude. Searchable's survey is based on eight million messages from an opted-in, anonymized US panel that were typed or spoken to ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude between September 2025 and September 2026. It found that chatbots resolved the initial complaint in their next response 24 percent of the time when insulted, compared to 35 percent when users refrained from insults. Men used a third more swear words than women did (22.0 per 10,000 words compared to 16.5), according to the survey, and age also influenced chatbot abuse, with people aged 35 to 44 outswearing those aged 18 to 24 (21.7 per 10,000 words compared to 13.3). Regionally, Nevada ranked as the meanest state, at 22.7 words per 10,000, while New Jersey was the most polite, at half Nevada's rate. How much of that sort of interaction might be tolerated? events.excerpt: Hi all, Happy to launch private.zecblock.com , a version of ZecBlock where the server doesn’t learn what you look up. ZecBlock Private uses PIR (Private Information Retrieval) . How it works Your browser encrypts the search before sending it. The transaction ID, block or address never leaves your device in readable form. The server works through the whole dataset to answer, without knowing which record you asked for. It sends back one encrypted answer, and only your browser can decrypt it. A search for something that exists looks the same as a search for something that doesn’t. As far as we know, it’s the first full block explorer (transactions, blocks and addresses) built on PIR. Previous PIR explorer demos covered narrower lookups, such as address balances. Check it yourself Open your browser’s developer tools (Inspect → Network) and search for something. Every request of the same kind is the same size, and none of them contains what you typed. After each search, the site also shows a short summary of exactly what your browser sent. Details Data stays close to the chain tip: new blocks are published every few seconds, typically within about 20 seconds of the regular explorer. Each data publication is signed, and your browser checks every result against it. Searches are heavier
events.headline: ZecBlock Private: look up transactions, blocks and addresses with PIR

events.excerpt: OpenAI has launched two new security products, one for penetration testing and another for defense, and warned organizations that their businesses are only safe if they use tools like these. “We're now at a point where companies will be secure only to the extent of the frontier model that they use to defend themselves and how well they utilize that,” OpenAI President Greg Brockman said during a Thursday keynote address. The co-founder of the company that broke security did admit that security “fundamentals are important, and not to be discounted.” However, “you need to really reorient your security practice around what these models can do,” Brockman said, with zero irony, and presumably talking about using AI models for defense - not for hacking other organizations . “Also very important is product.” This product, of course, should come from OpenAI, and, to that end, the company rolled out Daybreak Red Team and Daybreak Defense Factory, which are both part of OpenAI’s Daybreak security platform. Red Team , which is available in early access, uses OpenAI models to test companies’ web applications for vulnerabilities. events.excerpt: This release contains bugfixes and improvements to the stacks-node and stacks-signer binaries, ensuring more consistent block production. This release is compatible with chainstate directories from 4.0.x. This release is recommended for all Stacks node and signer operators. This release includes the following changes: https://github.com/stacks-network/stacks-core/blob/4.0.7/CHANGELOG.md Fixed Fixed nodes being unable to download a large Nakamoto tenure. A /v3/tenures response could hold up to 16 MiB of blocks, but the receiving node counts the response's chunk framing against the same limit and dropped the connection before the end, so a node that missed blocks in a tenure larger than about 16 MiB could never fetch them. /v3/tenures now leaves room for chunk framing so that nodes can read its responses. Docker images have been published to GitHub Container Registry: stacks-core Debian (glibc): https://github.com/stacks-network/stacks-core/pkgs/container/stacks-core/1552868085?tag=4.0.7 docker pull ghcr.io/stacks-network/stacks-core:4.0.7@sha256:a0d7dee7ab117de231d6dd659e777b2647c18bf2c29c8737c7be94980891ba0b Alpine (musl): https://github.com/stacks-network/stacks-core/pkgs/container/stacks-core/1552867423?tag=4.0.7-alpine docker pull ghcr.io/stacks-network/stacks-core:4.0.7-alpin

events.excerpt: Polymarket has laid off employees and ended several contractor agreements as part of a broader company restructuring. Cuts have mainly affected its marketing, customer experience, and engineering teams. The company said that the move comes as it prepares for its next phase of growth. Latest Shake-Up More than half of those affected were contractors, while some full-time employees were also let go, according to FOX Business. Polymarket also pushed back against reports claiming that around 30% of its workforce had been cut, and described that figure as inaccurate. However, the company has not shared how many employees or contractors were affected overall. The layoffs came into focus after an internal email informing contractors about the termination of their agreements started circulating on X. According to Reuters, the email stated that their contracts would end effective November 4, 2026, under a company-wide reduction in force. The email was specifically sent to contractors rather than full-time staff. The restructuring comes alongside several leadership changes at Polymarket. Warren Jenson joined as the company’s first chief financial officer in September, while former Uber executive Travis VanderZanden came on board as chief growth officer earlier this year. The Bigger Picture
events.headline: Polymarket Lays Off Employees and Ends Contractor Deals, Denies Reports of 30% Workforce Cuts

When the Chip Security Act was introduced, in May 2025, lawmakers said the technology to implement it existed, something Nvidia has not publicly confirmed.
